title: Your PCP Role: Scope, Medical Direction, and Duties
next: Chapter 2: The Well-Being of the Paramedic

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already follow protocols, keep the scene safe and hand over to the next level of care. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Where the PCP sits among Canada's four levels of care
  2. How medical direction works: direct, indirect, protocols, CPGs
  3. Your duties on every call, and the standards you're measured by

Textbook: Chapter 1, PDF pages 64–104
slides.say: Welcome to your first PCP class. You all hold an EMR licence, so you already know how an EMS system works from the inside. You follow protocols, you keep the scene safe, and you hand your patient over to the next level of care. Now you're becoming that next level. A PCP carries more delegated medical acts, makes more decisions, and is held to a higher standard. Today we'll cover three things. First, where the PCP sits among Canada's four levels of care, and what your licence really allows. Second, how medical direction works. And third, your duties on every call, and how your work is reviewed.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上第一堂 PCP 课。你们都持有 EMR 执照，所以对 EMS 系统的内部运作并不陌生：按协议做事、保障现场安全、把病人交给更高一级的照护。现在，你自己正在成为那「更高一级」。PCP 承担更多被委派的医疗行为，要做更多决定，标准也更高。今天讲三件事：第一，PCP 在加拿大四个执业层级里处于什么位置，你的执照到底允许你做什么；第二，医疗指导是怎么运作的；第三，你每次出车的职责，以及你的工作怎样被审查。

slides.title: From scoop and swoop to profession
slides.body:
Your licence is a privilege, not a right

  • Early EMS: "scoop and swoop" (load up and drive fast)
  • Today: assessment, treatment and clinical judgement
  • The NOCP lists the core competencies for Canadian paramedics
  • 2011: the NOCP became a foundation for a national exam
  • Many calls don't replace training: keeping current is on you
slides.say: In the early days, the job was called scoop and swoop: pick the patient up and drive fast to the hospital. That has changed a lot. Today, paramedics assess, treat, and make clinical decisions. The skills you're expected to master are listed in the NOCP, the National Occupational Competency Profile. In 2011, it was chosen as a foundation for developing a national paramedic exam. Remember this too: your licence is a privilege, not a right, and it comes with a duty to keep learning. Running lots of calls doesn't replace training. In the end, keeping your knowledge and skills current is your own responsibility.
slides.sayZh: 早期这份工作被叫作 scoop and swoop，「抬上车就跑」：把病人抬上车，飞快送医院。现在变化很大。今天的院前急救员要评估、处置、做临床决定。你需要掌握的能力都写在 NOCP，也就是《全国职业能力档案》里；2011 年，它被选作开发全国院前急救考试的基础文件。还要记住：执照是特权，不是权利，它带着持续学习的责任。出车多不能代替培训。说到底，让自己的知识和技能保持最新，是你自己的责任。

slides.title: Four levels of care in Canada
slides.body:
LevelWhat the textbook describes
EMRFirst responder: CPR and first aid
PCPThe backbone: oxygen, splints, select drugs, defibrillation; some IV
ACPALS: intubation, cricothyrotomy, needle decompression, more drugs
CCPCritical care transfers: blood products, ventilators

Each level has a scope of practice, and it is reviewed over time.
slides.say: Canada has four main levels of paramedic practice. The emergency medical responder, or EMR, is the first responder, trained in CPR and first aid, and often part of a fire service or another community agency. The PCP is the backbone of most systems. PCPs give oxygen, care for wounds, splint, give a select group of drugs for common problems like cardiac chest pain and shortness of breath, and defibrillate. Some PCPs also start IVs and use supraglottic airways. The ACP adds advanced airway skills like intubation and needle decompression, plus many more drugs. The CCP mainly moves critically ill patients between hospitals. Each level has a scope of practice, and it's reviewed over time.
slides.sayZh: 加拿大的院前急救主要分四个层级。急救医疗响应员 EMR 是第一响应者，接受过 CPR 和急救培训，常隶属消防或其他社区机构。PCP 是大多数系统的主力：给氧、处理伤口、上夹板，用少数几种药处理心源性胸痛、气促这类常见问题，还能除颤；部分 PCP 还能开静脉、使用声门上气道。ACP 增加了插管、针刺减压等高级气道技能，用药也多得多。CCP 主要负责在医院之间转运危重病人。每个层级都有自己的执业范围，而且会定期重新评估。

slides.title: Licensed, but not independent
slides.body:
Licencelegal permission to practisebefore it: practising medicine without a licence
Registrationa board keeps your training and licence recordsshows you passed provincial testing
Reciprocityanother province recognizes yourules differ by province

Even when licensed, you perform medical acts delegated by your medical director, within your scope.
slides.say: Let's sort out three words. Your licence, or certification, is legal permission to practise. Working as a paramedic before you have it counts as practising medicine without a licence. Registration means a recognized board keeps the records of your training, licence, and recertification, and it shows you passed the provincial testing. Reciprocity is when another province recognizes your licence, and each province sets its own rules. Now the key idea for a PCP: a licence does not make you independent. The medical acts you perform, such as giving a drug, are delegated to you by a physician medical director, and you work under that oversight.
slides.sayZh: 先把三个词理清楚。执照（或认证）是依法执业的许可；拿到之前就以院前急救员身份操作，等同无照行医。注册是指由认可的委员会保存你的培训、执照和再认证记录，也表明你通过了省级考试。互认是指另一个省承认你的执照，各省规则不同。对 PCP 来说关键是：执照不等于独立执业。你做的医疗行为，比如给药，是医生医疗主管委派给你的，你在这种监督下工作。

slides.q: An EMR colleague asks what you'll be able to do as a PCP. Which skill does the textbook place at the ACP level, not the PCP level?
slides.say: Let's check your understanding. An EMR colleague asks what you'll be able to do as a PCP. Which skill does the textbook place at the ACP level, not the PCP level? A, supraglottic airway. B, manual defibrillation. C, needle decompression. D, medication for ischemic chest pain. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来检查一下。一位 EMR 同事问你当了 PCP 以后能做什么。下面哪项技能书中归为 ACP，而不是 PCP？A 声门上气道；B 手动除颤；C 针刺减压；D 用药处理缺血性胸痛。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C, needle decompression. The textbook groups it with intubation and cricothyrotomy as advanced care paramedic skills, and in BC it is outside both EMR and PCP scope. A supraglottic airway, manual or automated defibrillation, and a select group of drugs for problems like ischemic chest pain are all described in the book as PCP-level care; the BC exam guidelines use the AED.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C，针刺减压。书中把它和插管、环甲膜切开一起列为 ACP 技能；在 BC，它也不属于 EMR 或 PCP 的执业范围。声门上气道、手动或自动除颤、以及用少数几种药处理缺血性胸痛等问题，书中都描述为 PCP 层级的照护；BC 考纲里用的是 AED。

slides.title: Medical direction: direct vs indirect
slides.body:
Direct medical controlIndirect medical control
Real time: radio, phone, electronicAway from the call
Orders for this patientProtocols and standing orders
Telemetry, live quality checkTraining, quality improvement
Can help on sceneReviews your PCRs

You are the medical director's eyes and hands on scene.
slides.say: Your medical director oversees your practice in two ways. Direct medical control happens in real time, by radio, phone, or another electronic link. You describe the patient and get specific orders for this patient. Indirect medical control happens away from the call: writing protocols and standing orders, training, quality improvement, and reviewing your patient care reports afterwards. As a PCP, more of your work involves delegated drugs and procedures, so knowing when to call for direct orders really matters. Think of yourself as the medical director's eyes and hands on scene. The clearer your report, the better the orders you'll get.
slides.sayZh: 医疗主管通过两种方式监督你的执业。直接医疗控制是实时的，通过无线电、电话或其他电子方式：你报告病人情况，得到针对这个病人的具体医嘱。间接医疗控制在出车之外进行：制订协议和常规医嘱、培训、质量改进，以及事后审阅你的病人护理报告。作为 PCP，你的工作里有更多被委派的药物和操作，所以知道什么时候该请求直接医嘱非常重要。把自己想成医疗主管在现场的眼睛和双手：你报告得越清楚，得到的医嘱就越好。

slides.title: Protocol, standing order, or CPG?
slides.body:
Protocoltreatment plan for one illness or injuryoften built on national standards
Standing ordersigned orders: what you may or must not do before callinge.g. defibrillation
CPGrecommendations you adapt to the patientneeds critical thinking

A CPG is the most flexible, so it leans hardest on your judgement.
slides.say: These three terms are often tested. A protocol is a treatment plan for a specific illness or injury, usually built on national standards, such as the Heart and Stroke Foundation's cardiac algorithms. A standing order is a type of protocol, written and signed by the medical director, that says what you may do, or must not do, before you contact direct medical control. Defibrillation is a classic example. A clinical practice guideline, or CPG, goes one step further. It gives recommendations, and you choose which parts fit this patient and this situation. That flexibility is exactly why a CPG demands strong critical thinking. The more freedom you're given, the more your judgement matters.
slides.sayZh: 这三个词常考。协议是针对某种疾病或损伤的处置计划，通常以国家标准为基础，比如加拿大心脏与卒中基金会的心脏急救流程。常规医嘱是协议的一种，由医疗主管书面签署，规定在联系直接医疗控制之前你可以做什么、不能做什么，除颤就是典型例子。临床实践指南，也就是 CPG，再往前一步：它给出建议，由你判断哪些部分适合眼前这个病人、这种情况。正因为灵活，CPG 特别需要批判性思维。给你的自由越多，你的判断就越重要。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Practise under protocols and medical oversight
  • Scene safety and PPE first
  • Primary survey, CPR and AED, oxygen, bleeding control
  • Clear handover; protect privacy
  • Write the PCR, a legal record

PCP adds

  • More delegated acts in BC: IV and fluids, CPAP, more drugs
  • More decisions, each followed by reassessment
  • Usually the team leader, guiding first responders
  • Knows what the first responders are trained to do
  • Plans the destination: right hospital, right resources
slides.say: The left side is the shared base you already know. You practise under protocols and medical oversight, put safety first, do the primary survey, CPR, oxygen, and bleeding control, hand over clearly, and write a patient care report. The right side is new. In BC, more acts are delegated to you, such as IV access and fluids, CPAP, and a longer drug list. You make more decisions, and every one needs a reassessment. The textbook says the paramedic is usually the team leader, so you'll guide the first responders on scene, and you need to know what they're trained to do. And you think ahead about destination: does this hospital have what this patient needs?
slides.sayZh: 左栏是你已经熟悉的共同基础：在协议和医疗监督下执业、安全第一、做初步评估、CPR、给氧、止血、清楚交接、写病人护理报告。右栏是新的。在 BC，委派给你的行为更多了，比如静脉通路和补液、CPAP，还有更长的药物清单。你要做更多决定，每个决定之后都要复评。书里说院前急救员通常是团队领导，所以你要在现场指导第一响应者，也要清楚他们受过什么培训。你还要提前考虑去向：这家医院有没有这个病人需要的资源？

slides.title: Your duties on every call
slides.body:
Prepare→Respond→Manage the scene→Assess and treat
Manage and choose destination→Hand over→Document→Return to service

Protocol doesn't fit, or you'd need to vary from it? Call medical direction.
slides.say: The textbook lists your responsibilities on every call as a sequence. Prepare: your body, your mind, your knowledge, and your equipment. Respond quickly but safely. Manage the scene: your own and your team's safety first, then the patient and bystanders. Assess and treat, starting with the most urgent problem. Then manage the patient under your protocols and choose the right destination. Hand over with a short, clear report. Document right away. And restock so the unit is ready. One point matters even more at PCP level: when the protocol doesn't cover the situation, or you think you need to vary from it, contact your medical director or direct medical control. Don't improvise.
slides.sayZh: 书里把你每次出车的职责列成一个顺序。准备：身体、心理、知识和设备都要到位。响应：要快，也要安全。现场管理：先保证自己和团队的安全，再是病人和旁观者。评估与处置：从最紧急的问题开始。然后按协议管理病人、选择合适的去向。交接：简短清楚。立即记录。最后补给整备，让车随时能出。有一点在 PCP 层级更加重要：协议不适用于眼前的情况，或者你认为需要偏离协议时，要联系医疗主管或直接医疗控制，不要临场发挥。

slides.q: You're the PCP on a call. A bystander says she is a physician and tells you to give a treatment your protocols don't allow. She is not your medical director. What should you do?
options: Follow her order, because a physician outranks you
Politely explain you follow your medical director's protocols; she can take over only if she accepts full responsibility and rides in with the patient
Ask the police to remove her from the scene right away
Give the treatment, and write in the PCR that she ordered it
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. You're the PCP on a call. A bystander says she is a physician and tells you to give a treatment your protocols don't allow. She is not your medical director. What should you do? A, follow her order, because a physician outranks you. B, politely explain that you follow your medical director's protocols, and that she can take over only if she accepts full responsibility and rides in with the patient. C, ask the police to remove her right away. D, give the treatment, and write in the report that she ordered it. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。你是现场的 PCP。一位旁观者说她是医生，要你做一项你的协议不允许的处置。她不是你的医疗主管。你该怎么做？A 照她说的做，因为医生级别比你高；B 礼貌地说明你按自己医疗主管的协议执行，只有她承担全部责任并随车到医院，才能接手；C 马上请警察把她带离现场；D 照做，然后在报告里写明是她下的指令。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Your delegation comes from your own medical director, so you stay within your local protocols and standing orders. An on-scene physician can take over care only by accepting full responsibility for the patient and staying with them all the way to the emergency department. A ignores where your authority comes from. C is unprofessional when she may simply be trying to help. D doesn't protect you: writing down her order doesn't put the act back inside your scope.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。你的授权来自你自己的医疗主管，所以要坚持本地协议和常规医嘱。现场医生只有承担病人的全部责任、并一路陪同到急诊科，才能接手照护。A 忽略了你的权限从哪里来；C 不专业，她可能只是想帮忙；D 保护不了你，把她的指令写下来，并不会让这项操作回到你的执业范围之内。

slides.title: Professionalism: integrity first
slides.body:
Integrity: the single most important trait

  • Be open, honest and truthful with patients
  • Empathy, self-motivation, plain-language communication
  • Lead the team: guide and support, never undermine
  • Advocate: the patient's interests and wishes first; keep privacy
  • Suspect abuse or neglect of a child, spouse or elder? Report it
  • First impressions form in about 10 seconds
slides.say: Patients judge you fast; the textbook says people form a first impression in about ten seconds. Clean uniform, clean hands, no dangling jewellery. But the trait the book calls the single most important is integrity: being open, honest, and truthful with your patients. Add empathy, a drive to keep improving, and plain language instead of medical jargon. As a PCP you'll usually lead the team, and a good leader guides and supports people rather than undermining them. You're also the patient's advocate. Put their interests and wishes first, even when they differ from yours, protect their privacy, and if you suspect abuse or neglect of a child, a spouse, or an older adult, report it.
slides.sayZh: 病人对你的判断很快，书里说第一印象大约在十秒内形成：制服干净、双手干净、不戴晃来晃去的首饰。但书里称为最重要的单项素养是诚信：对病人坦诚、诚实、真实。再加上同理心、不断进步的内在动力，以及用通俗语言而不是医学行话沟通。作为 PCP 你通常是团队领导，好的领导引导和支持队员，而不是拆台。你也是病人的代言人：把病人的利益和意愿放在首位，即使和你自己的想法不同；保护病人隐私；如果怀疑儿童、配偶或老人受虐或被忽视，要上报。

slides.title: Making care better: CQI
slides.body:
CQIreview everyday practice to prevent problemsongoing, system-wide
QAfind a problem, fix itafter something went wrong
Peer reviewcolleagues review callslearning tool, kept confidential
  • Report adverse events and near misses
  • Error disclosure: paramedics and medical director meet the family
slides.say: Good systems keep checking themselves. Continuous quality improvement, or CQI, reviews everyday practice to find system problems and prevent them. Quality assurance looks at a problem that has already happened and finds a fix. Many services run peer review, where colleagues review calls using consistent guidelines. When a reviewer finds something you can improve, treat it as a lesson, not an attack. When you review others, never use it to belittle anyone or discuss it outside the review team. As a professional, you also report adverse events and near misses, meaning errors that almost caused harm. Many provinces now have error disclosure, where paramedics and medical directors meet patients and families to discuss what went wrong.
slides.sayZh: 好的系统会不断自我检查。持续质量改进，也就是 CQI，审查日常做法，找出系统问题并预防它们。质量保证 QA 针对已经发生的问题，找出解决办法。很多机构用同行评审：同事按统一的标准审查出车记录。评审员指出你可以改进的地方时，把它当作学习，而不是攻击；你当评审员时，绝不能借此贬低别人，也不能在评审圈外讨论。作为专业人员，你还要上报不良事件和险兆事件，也就是差点造成伤害的差错。现在很多省有错误披露流程，院前急救员和医疗主管会与病人及家属面谈，说明出了什么问题。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A licence isn't independence: only delegated acts
  • Protocol doesn't fit? Call medical direction; don't improvise
  • On-scene doctor: keep to your protocols unless they take over fully
  • PCR right after handover: it's a legal record
  • Log equipment checks and repairs, too
  • Unit not restocked when the next call comes: legal risk
slides.say: Now the traps that grow as your scope grows. First, a licence is not independence. Every drug and procedure you use is delegated, so stay within your scope and protocols. Second, when the protocol doesn't fit the patient in front of you, don't improvise; contact medical direction. Third, an on-scene physician who isn't your medical director can't simply override your protocols. Fourth, complete the patient care report right after handover. It's the legal record of what you did. The textbook adds that documenting equipment checks and repairs is nearly as important. Finally, restock right away. If the next call comes and the unit isn't ready, there can be legal consequences.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲随着执业范围变大而变多的陷阱。第一，执照不等于独立：你用的每种药、每项操作都是委派的，所以要守在执业范围和协议之内。第二，协议不适合眼前的病人时，不要临场发挥，联系医疗指导。第三，不是你医疗主管的现场医生，不能直接推翻你的协议。第四，交接后马上完成病人护理报告，它是你所做处置的法律记录。书里还说，记录设备检查和维修几乎同样重要。最后，马上补给整备。下一个呼叫来了而车还没准备好，可能带来法律后果。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• BC EMRs have no IV access; vascular access is PCP-only
  • Needle decompression is outside EMR and PCP scope
  • Stopping a resuscitation on scene: consult medical oversight
  • Jurisprudence exam: 25 questions, 80% to pass, every level
  • PCP written exam: COPR (your EMR written was EMALB's)
  • Practical: 1 medical + 1 trauma; under 70% → another of that type
slides.say: Here's how BC frames this chapter for your exams. In BC, EMRs have no IV access; vascular access appears only in the PCP part of the protocols. Needle decompression is outside both EMR and PCP scope. The BC cardiac arrest guideline says to consult medical oversight before you stop a resuscitation on scene. Now the exams themselves. Every licence level writes the jurisprudence exam: twenty-five questions, eighty percent to pass. Your EMR written exam was run by the EMA Licensing Branch, but your PCP written exam is the COPR entry-to-practice exam. The practical has two scenarios, one medical and one trauma. Score under seventy percent on one, and you're assigned another of the same type.
slides.sayZh: 来看 BC 怎样把本章内容放进你的考试。在 BC，EMR 没有静脉通路权限，静脉通路只出现在协议的 PCP 部分。针刺减压在 EMR 和 PCP 的范围之外。BC 的心脏骤停流程规定，在现场终止复苏前要咨询医疗监督。再说考试本身：每个执照级别都要考法规考试，二十五题，八十分及格。你的 EMR 笔试由 EMA 执照处负责，但 PCP 笔试是 COPR 的入职考试。实操考两个场景，一个内科、一个创伤；某个场景低于七十分，就要再考一个同类场景。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Licensed isn't independent: your acts are delegated
  2. Direct = real-time orders; indirect = protocols, training, review
  3. Integrity first; PCR right after handover; restock fast

Next: Chapter 2, the well-being of the paramedic
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: your PCP licence lets you practise, but it doesn't make you independent. Every drug and procedure is delegated by your medical director, within your scope. Two: direct medical control means real-time orders for this patient; indirect control is the protocols, standing orders, training, and reviews behind them. Three: integrity comes first, and every call ends the same way, with a prompt patient care report and a restocked unit. Next lesson, Chapter 2, we'll talk about you: staying healthy, handling stress and grief, and protecting yourself from injury and infection. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，PCP 执照让你可以执业，但不等于独立：每种药、每项操作都由医疗主管在你的执业范围内委派。二，直接医疗控制是针对这个病人的实时医嘱；间接医疗控制是背后的协议、常规医嘱、培训和审查。三，诚信第一，而且每次出车都以同样的方式结束：及时完成病人护理报告，车辆补给到位。下节课，第二章，我们谈谈你自己：保持健康、应对压力和悲伤、防止受伤和感染。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
